question.problem:
$\,$ $0$ is not positive and $0$ is not negative.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,¬(0\text{ is not positive}\text{ and }0\text{ is not negative}) & ≡¬((0\text{ is not positive})∧(0\text{ is not negative})) \\  & ≡¬(0\text{ is not positive})∨¬(0\text{ is not negative}) \\  & ≡(0\text{ is positive})∨(0\text{ is negative}) \\  & ≡0\text{ is positive}\text{ or }0\text{ is negative}.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: $0$ is positive and $0$ is not negative
$0$ is not positive or $0$ is not negative
$0$ is positive or $0$ is not negative
